reader.requirement: At --std 85 OPEN I-O must refuse a file that cannot support sequential I-O-mode operations (status 37, VII.1.3.5 3d2). A successful OPEN I-O must allow both READ and REWRITE: WRITE is refused 48, REWRITE with no preceding READ is 43, and a REWRITE of a RECORD VARYING record to a different size is 44.

edition-consulted.switches: SharingFacilityInEffect picks '61' (2002+) or '30' (85) for a host sharing refusal; the GR16/GR17 write-capability '37' is the same at every edition

reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f19_01 covers OPEN I-O then READ and REWRITE on a fixed file; it does not cover the 37 refusal of a read-only file, WRITE in I-O mode (48), REWRITE without READ (43), RECORD VARYING REWRITE sizes (44), or a READ after the failed OPEN I-O

reader.notes: The write-capability question is asked once above the organizations: FileConnector.OpenOnceEntered calls HostFile.PermitsWrite for a present file in any mode but INPUT and answers '37'. The I-O arm opens a ReadWrite reader, so READ and REWRITE share one stream. The probe's read-only file was copied into the run directory with its read-only attribute kept.

refuter.evidence:
r17c.cob at --std 85: FD FL LINAGE IS 5 LINES (a level-2 SEQ form of 1985), OPEN OUTPUT, WRITE 'LIN001' and 'LIN002', CLOSE, OPEN I-O FL printed L-IO=00, then READ printed L-READ=00 '
LIN0' (not LIN001), REWRITE 'REW001' printed L-REW=00, and a later OPEN INPUT read L-R1=00 REW001 / L-R2=00 '01
LI'. od -c of the file after: 'REW0010 1
LIN002
' - the REWRITE overwrote the first line end and half of record 1, corrupting the file. Same bytes at --std 2023 (r17c-002). The mechanism: SequentialConnector.SelectLineEnd / IsRecordPrintStream make a LINAGE file (and any file written with ADVANCING) a text print stream (DOC-A.1-146 (c'); kb/Work PB1190 landing: 'a print file is written, not re-read as framed records'), while the I-O arm of OpenCore opens it as a fixed-record ReadWrite file with no test of that shape. r14d.cob shows the same for a non-LINAGE file written AFTER ADVANCING: IO-OPEN=00, IO-1=00 '[
ADV00]', REWRITE 00, file now 'REW0011
ADV002
'. GR17 requires that OPEN I-O 'must reference a file that supports the input and output operations that are permitted for a sequential file when opened in the I-O mode' and places it in open mode for both; VII.1.3.5 3d2 gives 37 for a file that does not. The implementation does neither: it admits OPEN I-O (00) on a medium whose READ does not deliver the written record and whose REWRITE does not replace it. The reader's probes used only plain fixed and RECORD VARYING files, never a LINAGE or ADVANCING-written file. kb/Work search (LINAGE/print with READ/I-O/REWRITE/read back): no note files this; PB1190 only asserts print files are not re-read. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR17 (the text is in GR17); OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 (GRL2.3d.2); OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 (GRL2.3d.3). Doubt stated: the READ misread is also visible on OPEN INPUT, so the root may be filed against READ / the print-stream representation; the GR17 failure is that OPEN I-O succeeds and REWRITE corrupts the file.
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (harm wrong-answer, data corruption; cause b, same at --std 2023): OPEN I-O of a sequential file with a LINAGE clause, or one written with an ADVANCING phrase, returns 00 although the implementation's text print stream cannot support sequential I-O-mode READ and REWRITE; READ delivers bytes that straddle line ends and REWRITE overwrites them. Either the open must be refused 37 (VII.1.3.5 3d2) for a print-stream medium, or READ and REWRITE must work by line.
